memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood - two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high. He overlaid it with pure gold, both inside and out, and made a gold moulding around it." - Exod 37:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The most sacred object in Israel's worship begins with the same plain material as everything else — acacia wood from the desert.

But notice the difference here. The frames of the tabernacle were overlaid with gold on the outside. The ark was overlaid "both inside and out." Even the surface no one would ever see was pure gold.

That detail is not decoration. It says something about the God who dwelt above this box: what He is on the inside is exactly what He is on the outside. There is no hidden self with God, no private character that differs from the public one. He is light, and in Him there is no darkness at all (1 John 1:5).

We are not naturally like that. Most of us maintain some gap between the visible surface and the interior. Jesus confronted this directly, calling out those who cleaned the outside of the cup while the inside stayed full of greed (Matt 23:25-26).

The good news is that God works from the inside out. He is not merely improving our surface; He is making us new (2 Cor 5:17), transforming us by the renewing of our minds (Rom 12:2).

Where is the gap in you between the outside and the inside?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where is the biggest gap between how you appear and who you really are?
2. What would change if the hidden parts of your life were gold too?
3. Are you asking God to improve your surface or renew your heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are the same inside and out. Work in the hidden places of my life until there is no gap. Amen.
